### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aff2fd6fa41533b4f08f01743882d53a4780a1ad` — the merge of head `9a610dc7157a35e3b9f241e3b28caa288b3f1818` into base `6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aff2fd6fa41533b4f08f01743882d53a4780a1ad && git checkout aff2fd6fa41533b4f08f01743882d53a4780a1ad
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb 9a610dc7157a35e3b9f241e3b28caa288b3f1818 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb && git merge --no-ff 9a610dc7157a35e3b9f241e3b28caa288b3f1818

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c290d3af7c52d019d1de1c09b6b0306f09700bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9a610dc7157a35e3b9f241e3b28caa288b3f1818`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/personal-views.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/attachments.ts

Inputs read: card #37352 (body and its four comments, the claim 7194367121 and its amendment 7194982901 among them), PR #37594 (body, five-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (`own-door-bridge.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** No schema, no authorable key, no request field moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the correct kind.
- **Published surface of `@objectstack/spec`: widened — right.** `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` gains two keys, `own_door_personal_view_delete` and `own_door_attachment_mutate`, in each of its four locales (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`). The constant's declared type and the export list do not change, which agrees with the diff carrying no `api-surface` or `export-origins` hunk.
- **Locale parity: holds.** Each of the four locale blocks carries both keys, so the catalog's own "every locale defines every key en defines" pin stays satisfied; `Test Core` is green on the head.
- **Override address: no new behaviour — right.** The two keys become spellable as `errors.own_door_*`, and the catalog header already says the bridge consults no `i18n` service, so no override is read for them. The header sentence stays true.
- **Wire of `@objectstack/runtime`: only the language of `error.message` moves — right.** On `DELETE /personal-views/:id` and on `DELETE` and `PATCH /attachments/:id`, the two `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` sentences now render in the catalog locale the request's top `Accept-Language` tag resolves to. An English request, a request with no header, a `*` header and a language the catalog lacks all read the sentence they read on `main`, byte for byte. Code, status, the slot, member and package names are unchanged and no `userMessage` is added, as the card requires.
- **`OwnDoorBridge` contract: unchanged.** The interface is not in the diff; the two frozen bridge constants each gain the already-declared optional `nounKey`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/37352-own-door-501-locale.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/runtime` patch. These are exactly the two packages the diff moves. With `Metadata-protocol: none` the level is `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3) — right. `Check Changeset` is green.
- Clause-②: yes (widening) — right. The published catalog gains keys and nothing is taken away. The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset body, and the card's claim was amended to the same value (7194982901) before this review.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, Spanish noun in the singular** (`el punto de acceso para eliminar y renombrar adjuntos`): accepted. The catalog's two Spanish sentences are singular, both verbs are served at one path, and the form matches `own_door_print` in the same locale.
- **Dev flag, English keeps the plural noun with `is`**: accepted as the card's own constraint (English byte-identical to today's `noun`). See N1.
- **Key names**: the card leaves them to the dev. Both follow the `own_door_` prefix of the existing noun key. Accepted.
- **`Skills-docs: none`**: confirmed by a search of the head tree; no page under `skills/` or `content/` names the own-door bridge or these sentences.
- **`open_questions`**: none on the card or the PR.
- **SQL push-down**: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.
- **Author**: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay note is owed.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts`** — judged against the card, the #37336 precedent it follows, and its first consumer, `notImplementedSentence` in `packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts` (read, not reviewed).

- The consumer renders the noun and the sentence with one and the same caller locale. Both new keys exist in all four locales, so the two halves always resolve to the same language: a sentence cannot come out half translated. A top tag the catalog lacks yields no locale for either half, so the whole sentence is English.
- The English of each key equals the bridge's `noun` character for character (`the personal view delete door`, `the attachment removal and rename doors`), which is what the `nounKey` jsdoc on `OwnDoorBridge` requires and what the card demands.
- The header jsdoc, sentence by sentence: the door placeholder "is the door's noun, itself a key of this catalog", now naming all three keys — true; "capitalized" — true, and a no-op for the Chinese and Japanese nouns; "a bridge that names no noun key keeps its English sentence" — still true of the mechanism, although no shipped bridge takes that arm any more.
- Terminology: the Chinese, Japanese and Spanish nouns use the platform's own labels for `sys_personal_view` and `sys_attachment` in each locale (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/`), and the same word for "door" that `own_door_print` uses in that locale. The Spanish nouns capitalise to `El punto de acceso …` and agree with `no está disponible`.
- Attempts to break it: a regional or base-language variant (`zh`, `ja`, `es-MX`) reaches the catalog locale through the platform's one locale ladder, for both halves alike; q-values are not negotiated, as the header documents; a plain header record and a fetch `Request` are both read by the consumer. None of these splits a sentence across two languages or changes an English answer.

**`packages/runtime/src/domains/personal-views.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/attachments.ts`** — each `nounKey` is spelled exactly as its catalog key, on the same object as the `noun` whose English it mirrors. Each one-line comment says what the field does and is accurate. The claim, the doors, the slot, the member and the producer are untouched, so the bridge's forwarding contract is unchanged.

Nit:

- N1 (nit) — the English attachment sentence reads "The attachment removal and rename doors is not available": a plural noun with a singular verb. It reads this way on `main` today, and the card requires the English to stay byte-identical, so the PR is right to keep it. Repairing it would change the wire English, the bridge's `noun` and the catalog's English value together, and belongs on a follow-up card if the maintainer wants it. Accepted deviation on this head.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gvxx96-37352`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**
